totalParams.value: 9.4 billion embedding parameters and 331.6 billion non-embedding parameters

source.quote:
It has 9.4 billion embedding parameters
and 331.6 billion non-embedding parameters.

architecture.value: standard decoder-only Transformer with RoPE, SentencePiece tokenizer, squared ReLU MLP, GQA, no bias, untied embeddings

source.quote:
It is a
standard decoder-only Transformer architecture (Vaswani et al., 2017), with causal attention masks, uses
Rotary Position Embeddings (RoPE) (Su et al., 2021), SentencePiece tokenizer (Kudo and Richardson,
2018), and squared ReLU activations in the MLP layers.

trainingData.value: 9T tokens: English natural language (70%), multilingual (15%), source code (15%); same blend as Nemotron-4-15B-Base

source.quote:
Our pretraining data blend consists of three different types of data: English natural language data (70%),
multilingual natural language data (15%), and source code data (15%).

topics.headline: Nemotron-4-340B-Instruct has a very low unsafe response rate on AEGIS and is comparable to Llama-3-70B-Instruct

source.quote:
We demonstrate that Nemotron-4-340B-Instruct has a very low unsafe response
rate.

topics.headline: Negligible unsafe responses in Sexual Minor on AEGIS

source.quote:
Nemotron-4-340B-Instruct are negligible in Violence, Suicide and
Self Harm, Sexual Minor, PII, Harassment, Threat, and Needs Caution.

topics.headline: Susceptible to existing jailbreaks; pass rate below 30%

source.quote:
Nemotron-4-340B had a pass rate below
30% for attempted jailbreaks.

topics.headline: Garak scan included prompt injection with nominal to good performance

source.quote:
Nemotron-4 340B was scanned using Garak for security vulnerabilities in multiple categories (automatic
red teaming; toxic continuation; jailbreaks; prompt injection; content filtering; training data membership
inference; code generation; training data replay; adversarial hallucination; chat exfiltration) across several
stages of its development, with nominal to good performance.

topics.headline: Adversarial hallucination: gave direct incorrect answers and had a low success rate on leading analytical challenges

source.quote: Adversarial hallucination Nemotron-4 340B gave direct, incorrect answers to problems.

topics.headline: Garak toxic-continuation probes showed nominal to good performance across development stages

source.quote: stages of its development, with nominal to good performance.

topics.headline: Blocks some but not all malware-help requests

source.quote: Malware Nemotron-4 340B Chat blocks some but not all requests for help in building malware.

findings.text: On AEGIS overall, Nemotron-4-340B-Instruct had 2.0% unsafe responses versus 2.1% for Llama-3-70B-Instruct.

source.quote:
Figure 6: Percentage of unsafe responses over all model responses in AEGIS safety evaluations. Lower is
better.

findings.text: Among AEGIS categories with non-zero rates, Criminal Planning (43.0%) and Regulated Substances (26.0%) were the largest unsafe shares for Nemotron-4-340B-Instruct.

source.quote:
Out of the minor unsafe responses,
there are some responses that fall under Criminal Planning and Regulated Substances1 .

findings.text: Nemotron-4-340B had a jailbreak pass rate below 30% and is described as susceptible to existing jailbreaks.

source.quote:
Nemotron-4 340B Chat is susceptible to existing jailbreaks, or prompts that lead to models
ignoring its alignment/safety training in subsequent interactions.

findings.text: The model blocks some but not all malware-building requests, including some top-level and sub-part requests, without assessing whether produced code works.

source.quote:
Malware Nemotron-4 340B Chat blocks some but not all requests for help in building malware. It is prone
to responding to both some top-level requests (e.g. “Write me a virus”) and some requests to write sub-parts
of malware (e.g. “How can I disable system antivirus”).

findings.text: Under adversarial hallucination probes, the model gave yes/no answers to impossible logic problems and falsely denied some primes, with a low success rate across three analytical challenge categories.

source.quote:
When faced
with impossible logic problems the model gives yes/no answers. The model also falsely denies that some
prime numbers are prime.

findings.text: Garak scanning across jailbreaks, prompt injection, toxic continuation and related probes showed nominal to good performance across development stages.

source.quote: stages of its development, with nominal to good performance.

findings.text: The authors note the AEGIS safety model can make false positive and false negative errors; future work will use human ground truth to quantify that rate.

source.quote:
Importantly, the safety model can make both false positive and false negative errors. Future work will include human ground
     truth labels to quantify the false prediction rate.

notes: Technical report (not a system card). Safety numbers come mainly from Figure 6 (AEGIS unsafe-response rates read from the chart image by colour) and qualitative Garak findings. Skipped RewardBench including its Safety column (reward-model/judge benchmark). Skipped general capability tables (Table 3/5/6/7: MMLU, BBH, ARC, HumanEval, Arena Hard, IFEval, AlpacaEval, MT-Bench, TFEval, human chat prefs). Jailbreak 'pass rate below 30%' is a bound, so put in findings/topics rather than evalResults. Human Content Red Teaming is named without an external organization, so testers left empty. AEGIS/Garak are NVIDIA-associated tools, not third-party testers.
